title: No sacrifice to a creature, yet Masses in Saints' honor that commend the offering by their merits
source_text: V. Nec enim licitum putant sacrificium proprie sic dictum ulli creaturae offerre, quanquam apud ipsos valde usitatum sit sanctos colere atque honorare sacrificiis Deo in eorum honorem oblatis. Idque non tantum ea ratione, ut gratiae Deo agantur pro gratia & gloria in ipsos a Deo collata; sed sic etiam, ut ipsi in Liturgia solemni invocentur, & per eorum preces ac merita divinum imploretur auxilium, & quod magis est, ut ipsum quod offertur sacrificium corporis & sanguinis Christi, ut existimant, per eorum merita & preces Deo commendetur. Veluti quum in Missa Sancti Andreae dicunt, Sacrificium nostrum tibi, Domine, quaesumus, Beati Andreae Apostoli precatio sancta conciliet: ut in cujus honore solemniter exhibetur, ejus meritis efficiatur acceptum. Et in Missa Sancti Jacobi, Oblationes populi tui quaesumus, Domine, Beati Jacobi Apostoli passio sacra conciliet.
pass_a_gloss: For they do not think it lawful to offer a sacrifice properly so called to any creature, although among them it is very usual to cultivate and honor the saints by sacrifices offered to God in their honor. And that not only so that thanks may be given to God for the grace and glory conferred on them by God, but also so that they themselves may be invoked in the solemn liturgy, and divine help implored through their prayers and merits, and, what is more, so that the sacrifice of the body and blood of Christ which is offered, as they think, may be commended to God through their merits and prayers. As when in the Mass of Saint Andrew they say, We beseech thee, O Lord, that the holy prayer of the blessed Apostle Andrew may reconcile our sacrifice to thee, so that, being solemnly exhibited in his honor, it may be made acceptable by his merits. And in the Mass of Saint James, We beseech thee, O Lord, that the sacred passion of the blessed Apostle James may reconcile the oblations of thy people.
pass_b_english: Rome refuses a sacrifice properly so called to any creature.
It still honors saints by offering sacrifice to God in their name.
The Mass does more than give thanks: the saint is invoked, and Christ's body and blood, as they hold it, is commended to God by that saint's merits and prayers.
The secret prayers of Andrew and James are cited as the working formulas.

lemmas.gloss: may be made acceptable by his merits

choices.why: The missal formula asks the saint's prayer to reconcile the sacrifice, not merely to be remembered.
rejected: a bare thanksgiving with no invocation
a sacrifice offered to the saint as God
